title: Punctuation and Cohesion in Formal Prose
titlePt: Pontuação e coesão na prosa formal
summary: Use commas, semicolons, dashes, and cohesive references to guide complex formal prose without ambiguity.

sections.heading: Commas with subordinate clauses and dislocation
sections.body: Portuguese commas mark syntactic structure, not just pauses. Initial subordinate clauses and dislocated topics usually take a comma; subject and verb should not be separated by a comma without a structural reason.

examples.pt: Quando a reunião terminou, todos saíram.
examples.en: When the meeting ended, everyone left.
That point, we already discussed yesterday.

examples.pt: Os alunos que entregaram o trabalho receberam nota.
examples.en: The students who submitted the assignment received a grade.

sections.heading: Semicolon for balanced argument
sections.body: The semicolon is useful between independent clauses that are closely related, especially before formal connectors such as **porém**, **portanto**, and **contudo**.

examples.pt: A proposta é viável; contudo, exige investimento.
examples.en: The proposal is viable; however, it requires investment.

examples.pt: Os dados são limitados; portanto, a conclusão deve ser cautelosa.
examples.en: The data are limited; therefore, the conclusion must be cautious.

examples.pt: Alguns defendem a mudança; outros preferem manter o modelo atual.
examples.en: Some defend the change; others prefer to keep the current model.

sections.heading: Cohesive reference
sections.body: Cohesion depends on clear reference. Pronouns and demonstratives must point to an identifiable noun or idea; otherwise, repeat or rephrase the noun.

examples.pt: A empresa revisou o contrato. Essa revisão reduziu os riscos.
examples.en: The company reviewed the contract. This review reduced the risks.

examples.pt: O relatório cita inflação e desemprego; este subiu, aquela caiu.
examples.en: The report mentions inflation and unemployment; the latter rose, the former fell.

examples.pt: A decisão foi publicada ontem, o que surpreendeu o setor.
examples.en: The decision was published yesterday, which surprised the sector.

sections.heading: Dashes, parentheses, and emphasis
sections.body: Dashes add emphasis or interruption; parentheses add secondary information. In formal prose, use both sparingly so the main sentence remains readable.

examples.pt: O resultado — embora preliminar — é promissor.
A medida foi aprovada pelo conselho (com duas abstenções).
examples.en: The measure was approved by the board (with two abstentions).

examples.pt: O problema não é técnico — é político.
examples.en: The problem is not technical—it is political.

keyPoints: Punctuation should reflect syntax and logic, not only breath pauses.
Do not separate subject and verb with a comma in a simple sentence.
Semicolons help organize formal contrast and consequence.
Dashes and parentheses are effective when used sparingly.

commonMistakes.note: Do not separate subject and verb with a comma.

commonMistakes.wrong: A proposta é viável, contudo exige investimento.
commonMistakes.right: A proposta é viável; contudo, exige investimento.
commonMistakes.note: Formal connectors between clauses often work well after a semicolon.
If isso is unclear, name the referent.
